record.question:
A photo-sharing mobile application will serve millions of users. An existing backend authenticates users and maintains a trusted mapping from each user to an S3 object prefix. Mobile clients must upload and download directly from S3, and long-term AWS keys must not be embedded in the app. Bucket policies do not grant users additional access.

Which credential flow should the company implement?

options.text: Have the backend validate the user and request a short-lived STS role session with a session policy restricted to that user's prefix. Return the temporary credentials and obtain a new authorized session before they expire.
Create one IAM user with access to every user prefix and embed its access key and secret key in the app. Use the app interface to hide other users' objects.
Have the backend issue STS credentials at registration and store that one credential set permanently in the app, without implementing credential renewal.
Create a separate IAM user for every registered mobile user and provision long-term access keys into each installation of the app.

explanation.text:
<<1>> is correct. Authentication establishes the user, and the backend's trusted mapping determines the permitted S3 prefix. The backend assumes an authorized role with a session policy that narrows access for that session. The mobile client receives an access key, secret key and session token, then uses those temporary credentials for direct S3 requests.

<<2>> exposes shared credentials with access to all users' data; interface restrictions do not enforce S3 authorization. <<3>> fails after the credentials expire: STS credentials cannot be made permanent by storing them. <<4>> creates a large population of long-lived IAM credentials and does not satisfy the prohibition on embedding such keys.

A new session requires a fresh authorization decision based on the user's current access. Temporary credentials still need protection on the device. Session policies limit the role's existing permissions; they do not grant permissions that the role lacks.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_use-resources.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole.html

diagram_alt: Temporary mobile sessions permit scoped S3 access until expiration and require renewed authorization for replacement credentials.

sources.supports: Temporary credentials include a session token, expire, and must be replaced by a new credential set.
A session policy narrows the role session and cannot expand role permissions.
